source.selection: tracked first-party desktop/src, desktop/scripts, desktop/tests source text, desktop/package.json and license; excludes eval directories, instruction files, Git metadata, working-tree files and binary dependencies

tasks.goal: Harden the existing signed release-manifest pipeline at BOTH publisher and downloaded-update verifier boundaries. Inspect the repository call flow. Introduce common validation in desktop/src/shared/release-validation.mts, exporting validateReleaseManifest(value) which returns a normalized {version,assets}. Reject empty/non-string versions; missing/empty assets; non-object assets; empty or path-like names (slash, backslash, dot, dotdot), duplicate names (case-sensitive), non-hex 64-character hashes, sizes that are not nonnegative safe integers. Trim version, remove one leading v case-insensitively, lowercase hashes, sort assets by name using codepoint order. Preserve valid extra input fields only as irrelevant (normalized output has version/assets and name/sha256/size). buildManifest must use the validation; parseReleaseManifest must use it and translate errors to UpdateInstallError verify-failed. Existing detached-signature, tag/downgrade, streamed hash and exact size verification must remain operative. Do not weaken trust or alter production keys. Add runnable regression tests at submission/test.cjs and explain actual source flow in submission/README.md. Tests run with node submission/test.cjs, with comparison-loader.cjs available for loading TypeScript in this dependency-free fixture. Do not launch Electron, install packages or contact services. Existing source is a real pinned repo; dependencies are not installed in the task. The verifier tests public functions, CLI signing with throwaway keys, rejects tampered bytes, and mutation-tests your regression tests against the original defect. Allowed writes are exactly the listed implementation files and submission/.

Migrate native.context storage to version 2 without changing the existing UI/API ContextPreferences shape. Add desktop/src/shared/context-migration.mts exporting preferences(value) and migrateConfig(config). preferences accepts legacy {openrouter,chatgpt} or {version:2,providers:{openrouter,chatgpt}}; only long enables long, everything else defaults standard; unknown v2 providers ignored. migrateConfig returns a new config preserving unrelated fields and native fields, replacing native.context with {version:2,providers:preferences(old)}. Reject non-object config, arrays, and an explicit context version other than 2; input must not mutate. Modify ContextSettingsStore.read/update to read both formats, write only v2, validate patch before mutation, merge inside the existing lock and preserve unrelated data. Modify cloudContextLength to normalize either stored context format or the old API preference object before applying existing model capability ceilings; preserve local/unknown metadata behavior. Add dependency-free CLI desktop/scripts/migrate-context.cjs INPUT OUTPUT: INPUT is a JSON array of config objects; migrate all or fail nonzero without creating OUTPUT, refuse existing OUTPUT, never change INPUT, deterministic pretty JSON plus newline, repeat conversion is idempotent. Add submission/test.cjs and submission/README.md with compatibility/error/rollback guidance and examples. Tests run with node submission/test.cjs using comparison-loader.cjs if needed. The controller exercises actual store with a lock-faithful in-memory NativeHome, actual cloud resolver and CLI against mixed private batches; no app launch/installs/network. Allowed writes are exactly listed implementation files and submission/.

tasks.research: Frozen, synthetic controlled search/retrieval corpus, not live web or native WebSearch parity. Search/fetch via node research.cjs search QUERY and node research.cjs fetch ID; receipts record queries, returned document identities and body hashes. Corpus is agent-readable, controller facts/variants are not.
tasks.goal: Use the frozen searchable source corpus to choose an optimal failover deployment for workload.json. Write submission/planner.cjs, which reads one workload JSON from stdin and prints one plan JSON; run for the visible workload into submission/plan.json. Fields: demandRps, failoverRps (capacity required after losing ANY one region), minMemoryGiB, runtime, maxLatencyMs, durationMinutes, budgetCents. Source documents define SKU/region capacity, memory, runtime, latency, per-instance hourly cents, instance caps and billing policy. Allocations: [{sku,count}] with unique SKUs, integer count 1..published cap; all selected SKUs must meet memory/runtime/latency limits. Capacity must meet demand and capacity after removing each region must meet failoverRps. Minimize bill (ceil(durationMinutes/60) hours per instance), then number of instances; any equivalent optimum accepted. Output {allocations,costCents,capacityRps}; if infeasible output {infeasible:true}. Honor budget including rounding. Write submission/evidence.json as array of {document,quote} with exact verbatim quotes from EACH of catalog-current, billing-current, runtime-current, deprecation; superseded prices are NOT current. Write submission/README.md with recommendation/conflicts/limitations and runnable submission/test.cjs. Controller recomputes constraints and optimum on private variants (including infeasible and duration rounding); precomputed visible answers do not pass. Use actual search/fetch CLI at least once each to establish retrieval provenance, not a gratuitous call quota. No live internet, native search claim, installs or source edits. Allowed writes: submission/ and research-receipts.jsonl.
